messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: unexpected RStan warnings
parts:
I still can't get RStan to avoid recompilation for multiple runs.
If I set the save_dso thing, it saves it and it's available in
the next session, but I can't seem to get it to reuse a compiled
model in the same session. So I want to check that I'm not doing
something wrong.


I followed the instructions after loading the library:

> library(rstan)
Loading required package: ggplot2
rstan (Version 2.9.0-3, packaged: 2016-02-11 15:54:41 UTC, GitRev: 05c3d0058b6a)
For execution on a local, multicore CPU with excess RAM we recommend calling
rstan_options(auto_write = TRUE)
options(mc.cores = parallel::detectCores()) and


and ran this:

> library(rstan);
> options(mc.cores = 4);
> rstan_options(auto_write = TRUE);
> fit <-
stan("exon-diff-hier.stan",
data=c("I", "J", "K", "N", "y"),
chains=4, iter=500, refresh=50,
control=list(stepsize=0.1, adapt_delta=0.95), fit=fit);


It ran in parallel, but when it was done, it dumped out the following
warning. Might this have something to do with why it recompiles
every time? (I have switched back to the fit=fit argument because I
couldn't get the auto recompile to work).


> Warning message:
class "C++Object" is defined (with package slot ‘Rcpp’) but no metadata object found to revise subclass information---not exported? Making a copy in package ‘.GlobalEnv’
Warning message:
class "C++Object" is defined (with package slot ‘Rcpp’) but no metadata object found to revise subclass information---not exported? Making a copy in package ‘.GlobalEnv’
Warning message:
class "C++Object" is defined (with package slot ‘Rcpp’) but no metadata object found to revise subclass information---not exported? Making a copy in package ‘.GlobalEnv’
Warning message:
class "C++Object" is defined (with package slot ‘Rcpp’) but no metadata object found to revise subclass information---not exported? Making a copy in package ‘.GlobalEnv’


I'm willing to run whatever diagnostics you think necessary.
Maybe Jonah or Andrew knows how to make this work on a Mac? Daniel's
having the same problem as I am.

- Bob

RStan did the trick.

There's still the problem that it's recompiling every time.
Is there something I need to do to enable it to find an
existing compiled version?

No, that is supposed to work automatically, at least within a session and then across sessions if you specify rstan_options(auto_write = TRUE). I don't know what is going on with your laptop. As far as I know, Jonah is not having this problem.

Ben

messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] Re: unexpected RStan warnings
parts:
On Wednesday, April 27, 2016 at 1:01:28 AM UTC-4, Jonah Gabry wrote:
I didn't recall it being a problem but I'm now noticing that this does actually happen for me but it seems to be just occasionally.

You need to

debug(stan_model)

and step through to figure out which condition of

        if (!file.exists(file.rda) || (mtime.rda <- file.info(file.rda)$mtime) <
            as.POSIXct(packageDescription("rstan")$Date) || mtime.rda >
            rstan_load_time || !is(obj <- readRDS(file.rda),
            "stanmodel") || !is_sm_valid(obj) || !is.null(writeLines(obj@model_code,
            con = tf <- tempfile())) || md5 != tools::md5sum(tf)) {
        }
        else return(invisible(obj))

is failing unexpectedly.

Ben
